original_value: The classification and segmentation of large-scale, sparse, LiDAR point cloud with deep learning are widely used in engineering survey and geoscience. The loose structure and the non-uniform point density are the two major constraints to utilize the sparse point cloud. This paper proposes a lightweight auxiliary network, called the rotated density-based network (RD-Net), and a novel point cloud preprocessing method, Grid Trajectory Box (GT-Box), to solve these problems. The combination of RD-Net and PointNet was used to achieve high-precision 3D classification and segmentation of the sparse point cloud. It emphasizes the importance of the density feature of LiDAR points for 3D object recognition of sparse point cloud. Furthermore, RD-Net plus PointCNN, PointNet, PointCNN, and RD-Net were introduced as comparisons. Public datasets were used to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results showed that the RD-Net could significantly improve the performance of sparse point cloud recognition for the coordinate-based network and could improve the classification accuracy to 94% and the segmentation per-accuracy to 70%. Additionally, the results concluded that point-density information has an independent spatial–local correlation and plays an essential role in the process of sparse point cloud recognition.

result.paraphrase: Deep learning-based classification and segmentation of large-scale sparse LiDAR point clouds are widely applied in engineering surveying and geoscience. The loose structure and non-uniform point density are the two main constraints on using sparse point clouds. To address these issues, this paper presents a lightweight auxiliary network called the rotated density-based network (RD-Net) and a new point-cloud preprocessing method, Grid Trajectory Box (GT-Box). By combining RD-Net with PointNet, high-precision 3D classification and segmentation of sparse point clouds were achieved. The work highlights the importance of LiDAR point density features for 3D object recognition in sparse point clouds. In addition, RD-Net together with PointCNN, PointNet, PointCNN, and RD-Net were used as comparison methods. Public datasets were employed to evaluate the proposed approach. The results showed that RD-Net can substantially improve sparse point-cloud recognition performance for coordinate-based networks, raising classification accuracy to 94% and segmentation per-accuracy to 70%. The results also indicate that point-density information has an independent spatial-local correlation and plays a crucial role in sparse point-cloud recognition.
